db9f16e7: Quit the routine if there are no more actions to execute.
7108661d: Increment the action counter before executing the next action.
193472a9: Jump to the next action in the list.
fb414af3: If the current action is a 'RECOMPUTE' action, go to the previous action if the current field value is defined, otherwise execute the WRITE and TRANSPORT actions.

1d21d204: If the user did not enter any value, check if the current field is required, if the value should be deleted, or if a new entry should be created. If none of these conditions are met, go back to the beginning.
28a96123: If the user entered a '?', go to the QUERY action. If the user entered '^', execute the DELETE action and go to the '^DIE17' routine.
c9eb915c: If the user entered '@', execute the DELETE action and go to the 'Z^DIE2' routine.

8ce984bf: If the user entered a space, and the current field has a default value defined and is not a POINTER or VARIABLE POINTER field, set the user's input to the default value. If the field is not a DATE/TIME or SET OF CODES field, display the default value.

46999570: If the current action is not a WORD-PROCESSING field, go to the 'M^DIE17' routine. If it is a VARIABLE POINTER field, go to the '^DIE3' routine. If it is not a SET OF CODES field, go to the 'P' label. If the field has a CROSS-REFERENCE, execute it. Check if there is a syntax definition for the user's input, and if so, execute it. If the user's input is valid, display it, otherwise go to the 'V' label.
ca22d708: If the input Y has the delimiter colon and filter condition DIC("S") exists, execute the filter condition.
7f248875: If the local variable DB(DQ) is undefined, write the substring of YS starting from the position DG until the end. Set X to the portion of YS before the colon delimiter.

60d4ab4b: If the input variable DV contains the string "P", set up DIC and DIC(0) variables for call to the ^DIC routine, which is used for lookup and file operations. If DV does not contain "*", call ^DIC and set X to the internal entry number. If X is negative, go to the label X.
4878a4c1: If DV does not contain "N", call the tag D (presumably for data validation). If the decimal portion of X is longer than 24 characters, kill X and go to the label Z.
a4434f8e: Strip leading zeros from the numeric portion of a decimal value, and remove any trailing decimal point if the decimal portion is blank.
4dea839e: This line deletes the variable YS and sets V to one of two possible values: "@" (if DQ is undefined) or the value of the parameter array X(DQ).

4acfc600: This line clears the DIC("S") and DLAYGO arrays. If X is defined and not equal to the up-arrow character (^), it stores the value of X in DG(DW) and, if DV contains the letter "d", also stores X in ^DISV(DUZ,"DIE",DLB). It then branches to the label A.
048de7b6: This line writes the "??" characters to the current device and, if DB(DQ) is defined, branches to the Z^DIE17 label.
f7e86443: This line sets X to the string value "?BAD".
7873edea: This line sets the variable DZ to the current value of X, calls the D and QQ^DIEQ routines, and then branches to the label B.
84a9baf1: This line sets the D variable to the value of DIFLD, sets DQ(DQ) to a concatenation of DLB, DV, DU, DW, and the second through last pieces of the X_DQ routine. It then quits (returns).

8435ae72: If DE(DQ) is not defined, this line calls the O routine, then branches to the RD label if X is not equal to "@", to the A label if DV does not contain "R" and X is "@", or to the X label if X is "@". If reached, it sets X to the value of Y and branches to the N label.
89137e83: Executes code stored in the DD array for the current data dictionary entry.

0667e266: If processing a pointer field, and the pointed-to file exists, sets X to the internal entry number of the pointed-to entry. If the pointed-to entry exists in the file specified by the current data dictionary entry, sets Y to the .01 field value of the pointed-to entry and X and DG to the .01 field specifier (data type and label) of the current data dictionary entry.

740fb1fd: If processing a variable pointer field and the pointed-to file exists, sets X to the internal entry number of the pointed-to entry. If the pointed-to entry exists in the file specified by the current data dictionary entry, sets Y to the .01 field value of the pointed-to entry. If the current data dictionary entry has a .01 field, sets DG to the data type of the .01 field and X to the label of the .01 field specifier.
404c142e: Removes the semicolon prefix and the specified string (Y) from the input string (X), if it exists. Assigns the resulting string to Y if it is not empty.
